author: kleinesfilmroellchen
body:
### fix: ignore spurious zero-sized window buffers

winit+x11 usually supplies a single redraw event where the window’s backing buffer is still size zero. ignoring this case stops the event handler thread from panicking.

### fix: use physical size for winit window

physical size is needed since our raw framebuffer work doesn’t care about logical pixels and associated DPI scaling. with logical size, the window is too large (or even too small) for the area that is actually used for the framebuffer.

author: kyl191
body:
Request generation has output like
```
TASK [ansible-role-openvpn : server_keys | Generate CA key] ********************
task path: /etc/ansible/roles/ansible-role-openvpn/tasks/server_keys.yml:33
changed: [localhost] => {"changed": true, 
"cmd": ["openssl", "req", "-nodes", "-newkey", "rsa:2048", "-keyout", "ca-key.pem", "-out", "ca-csr.pem", "-days", "3650", "-subj", "/CN=OpenVPN-CA-localhost/"], 
"delta": "0:00:00.040497", 
"end": "2024-12-29 00:48:45.248738", 
"msg": "", 
"rc": 0, 
"start": "2024-12-29 00:48:45.208241", 
"stderr": "Ignoring -days without -x509; not generating a certificate\n
...
```

Similar problem also showed up in https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh-packages/issues/2661, they reference [req](https://linux.die.net/man/1/req) which does say `-days` is used with `-x509`.

Drop the `-days` from the key creation.

And move the long lines to use the `argv` parameter in the ansible command plugin.

author: aryamanarora
body:
this adds the method Neel suggested to me at NeurIPS. in general, I think this method is still sus because it seems to accidentally catch lots of high-activation latents that appear on very common tokens. some of the ones I noticed in my small-scale tests are
- [4392](https://www.neuronpedia.org/gemma-2-2b/10-gemmascope-res-16k/4392) "words related to magic or illusion"
- [6710](https://www.neuronpedia.org/gemma-2-2b/10-gemmascope-res-16k/6710) "references to errors and exceptions in programming contexts" (all programming-related features seem to get this one)

probably we need to adjust by activation density; coarse-grained features seem too favoured in this setup. generally, it seems non-trivial to do feature selection on an SAE.

This pull request introduces several enhancements and bug fixes to the `react-gridstack` components in the `dashboard` section of the application. The changes include adding new drag and resize event handlers, updating context types, and improving the animation of grid items during drag operations.

Enhancements to event handling and context:

* `apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-context.tsx`: Added new state variables `isDraggingId` and `isResizingId` to the `GridStackContext` and updated the `GridstackProvider` to manage these states. ([apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-context.tsxL6-R27](diffhunk://#diff-abf488f78ba4db9af283d15b0670ce59872cc1c463594f0bfb763ca94501bc8eL6-R27), [apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-context.tsxL31-R57](diffhunk://#diff-abf488f78ba4db9af283d15b0670ce59872cc1c463594f0bfb763ca94501bc8eL31-R57))
* `apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-grid.tsx`: Added new props `onItemDragStart` and `onItemDragStop` for handling drag events and updated the `GridstackGrid` component to handle these events and update context states accordingly. ([apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-grid.tsxR24-R25](diffhunk://#diff-e296419bee371c0351d3a10beae0e0d16921d146f932ebc1b70960eb1e551787R24-R25), [apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-grid.tsxR34-R37](diffhunk://#diff-e296419bee371c0351d3a10beae0e0d16921d146f932ebc1b70960eb1e551787R34-R37), [apps/web/src/app/[lang]/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/react-gridstack/gridstack-grid.tsxR54-R87](diffhunk://#diff-e296419bee371c0351d3a10beae0e0d16921d146f932ebc1b70960eb1e551787R54-R87))

author: thockin
body:
I noticed that when I manually ran "go generate" for the output_tests, it changed the result in metadataname.  The reason was that the command does not include metav1 when run this way, but when run from update-codegen, it does.

I figured that test was not proving much that the validatefalse test did not, so changed it to use a non-included pkg (which was not covered by a test) and lo and behold -- a bug!

We need to emit subfield validations before looking at whether the node is nil.

I renamed the test case, too.

author: bohyunshin
body:
## 변경점
* cuda out of memory가 발생해서 epoch을 돌면서 사용하지 않은 tensor을 삭제합니다.
* enum으로 두가지 metric을 추가합니다.
  * 근처 식당을 필터링하지 않는 경우: `Metric enum` (ap, map, ndcg, recall)
    * 이 경우는 유저 a에 대해서 top k 추천을 일괄적으로 하는 경우 입니다. (강남 음식점이든, 속초 음식점이든 상관 x)
  * 근처 식당을 필터링하는 경우: `NearCandidateMetric enum` (ranked_prec, recall)
    * 이 경우는 유저 a의 현위치를 평점을 방문한 식당의 위도, 경도로 가정하여 인근 1km 식당 대상으로 추천을 하는 경우 입니다.

## python 실행 코드
```bash
$ python3 embedding/node2vec.py \
    --batch_size 128 \
    --embedding_dim 32 \
    --walk_length 20 \
    --context_size 10 \
    --walks_per_node 10 \
    --p 1 \
    --q 0.5 \
    --num_negative_samples 20 \
    --model_path node2vec.pt \
    --log_path node2vec.log \
    --epochs 10 \
    --data_obj_path data_obj.pkl
```

* q값을 더 줄여서 bfs 보다는 dfs에 더 가까운 sequence을 생성하고자 했습니다.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change replaces all new instances of `java.util.Random` with the marginally slower, but much more secure `java.security.SecureRandom`.

We have to work pretty hard to get computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `java.util.Random` type uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and our changes all look something like this:

```diff
- Random r = new Random();
+ Random r = new java.security.SecureRandom();
```

body:
This change replaces the usage of [`java.io.File#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/io/File.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)) with [`java.nio.file.Files#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/file/Files.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute...)) which has more secure attributes.

The `java.io.File#createTempFile()` method creates a file that is world-readable and world-writeable, which is almost never necessary. Also, the file created is placed in a predictable directory (e.g., `/tmp`). Having predictable file names, locations, and will lead to many types of vulnerabilities. History has shown that this insecure pattern can lead to [information leakage](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-28168/), [privilege escalation](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-29428/) and even [code execution](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2022/02/25/3).

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
+  import java.nio.file.Files;
   ...
-  File txtFile = File.createTempFile("acme", ".txt");
+  File txtFile = Files.createTempFile("acme", ".txt").toFile();
```

author: marcoeilers
body:
This PR adds consistency checks that forbid inhale-exhale assertions in predicate bodies and in function preconditions. Currently, Silicon raises an internal error when it encounters these (see https://github.com/viperproject/silicon/issues/271), whereas Carbon just accepts them.

I think the semantics is at the very least completely unclear and probably doesn't make sense at all, which is why this PR forbids this situation for now. However, this obviously needs to be discussed first, so this PR should not be merged before it's been discussed in a Viper meeting.

author: pointbazaar
body:
Shrinking the IR. This simplifies the compiler and makes it easier to port to other architectures.

TAC_BINARY_OP_IMMEDIATE can always be replaced by
a sequence of

  TAC_CONST_VALUE
  TAC_BINARY_OP

e.g. 't3 += 2' -> 't4 = 2; t3 += t4'
e.g. 't3 |= 5' -> 't4= 5; t3 |= t4'

In the short term, this will probably increase the size of assembly code that's emitted.

### General:

-   [ ] The pull request title is descriptive. _(ex. `Added Lunar Network`, not `Updated metadata.json`)_
-   [ ] The pull request does not contain any unrelated commits. _(ex. commits from previous pull requests)_

### Mapping Additions or Updates:

-   [ ] Folder with appropriate name has been created / updated (must not include any non-alpha characters or whitespace).
-   [ ] No changes were made to the file's formatting (4 spaces per tab).
-   [ ] There are no syntax errors.
-   [ ] There is no pre-existing mapping matching my id (check if there is an existing folder).
-   [ ] My field values match your requirements.
-   You can view our patterns here: [metadata.schema.json](https://github.com/LunarClient/ServerMappings/blob/master/metadata.schema.json), or take a look below and complete the field checklist:
    -   [ ] `id`: a lowercase string, which should match the folder name _(ex. `myserver`)_
    -   [ ] `name`: a string _(ex. `MyServerPvP`)_
    -   [ ] `description`: hook between 16 and 80 characters in English _(ex. `Home of Competitive Minecraft PvP`)_
    -   [ ] `addresses`: an array with lowercase strings _(ex. `["my.server", "your-server.com"]`)_
        -   You do not need to specify subdomains, Lunar Client services automatically detect them.
    -   [ ] `primaryAddress`: the primary address that people connect to with (please include the subdomain if required) _(ex. `mc.my.server`)_
    -   [ ] `minecraftVersions`: an array with Minecraft versions as strings _(ex. `["1.18._", "1.19.2"]` - Must be versions or subversions supported by Lunar Client)\*
    -   [ ] `primaryMinecraftVersion`: a Minecraft version as a string _(ex. `1.19.2` - Must be a subversion supported by Lunar Client)_
    -   [ ] `primaryColor`: a hexademical color code that primarily distinguishes the server _(ex. `#00FFFF`)_
    -   [ ] `secondaryColor`: a hexademical color code that accompanies the `primaryColor` of the server _(ex. `#FF0000`)_
    -   [ ] `primaryRegion`: the primary region where your server operates in _(ex. `NA`)_
    -   [ ] `regions`: a list of regions where you have servers located that service your players _(ex. `["NA", "EU", "AS"]`)_
    -   [ ] `gameTypes`: a list of games that describe the content on your server, must be a max of 3 listed _(ez. `["PVP", "UHC", "HCF"]`)_
    -   [ ] `crossplay`: whether the server has support for Bedrock Edition players (through proxies such as [GeyserMC](https://geysermc.org/))
    -   [ ] (optional) `presentationVideo`: YouTube video ID (in slug) to server trailer / introduction _(ex. `7EV4cPuJvXE`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `votingLinks`: an array of urls to your server's listing on voting websites _(ex. `["https://minecraft-mp.com/server-s179012"]`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `website`: url of server website, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://www.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `store`: url of server store, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://store.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `wiki`: url of server wiki, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://wiki.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `merch`: url of server merchanise site (if seperate from store), must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://merch.your-server.com`)_

### Socials

-   [ ] (optional) `twitter`: username of twitter account without the @ _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `discord`: invite link to discord _(ex. https://discord.com/invite/4ceEJuH)_
-   [ ] (optional) `youtube`: slug or username of youtube channel _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `instagram`: username of instagram account _(ex. MyServer)_

-   [ ] (optional) `facebook`: slug of facebook page _(ex. MyServer)_

### Compliance

-   [ ] (optional) `privacyPolicy`: url to your Privacy Policy _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/privacy)_
-   [ ] (optional) `termsOfService`: url to your Terms of Service _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/terms)_
-   [ ] (optional) `rules`: url to your Rules _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/rules)_
-   [ ] (optional) `support`: url to your Support Site _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/support)_

### Media:

#### Logo

-   [ ] My logo is a `png` file.
-   [ ] I have uploaded my logo to my server folder _(ex. `lunarnetwork`)_ and named it `logo.png`.
-   [ ] My logo has a transparent background and is square (1:1 aspect ratio).

-   [ ] My logo is my own property and complies with relevant copyright/privacy laws.

#### Background

-   [ ] My background contains relevant content pertaining to the server, is my own property, and complies with relevant copyright/privacy laws.
-   [ ] My background doesn't contain any markings, text, or logos (unless part of a build).

body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/401ce15e-1a74-41a5-b4ad-635cb5b9dddc

Closes https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/issues/8899, https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/discussions/10281

Historically we haven't wanted to add this because querying OS theme preference required bringing in a bunch of platform-specific deps. A relatively recent [VT extension](https://github.com/contour-terminal/contour/blob/master/docs/vt-extensions/color-palette-update-notifications.md) originally proposed by the Contour terminal emulator though lets us query for the terminal's theme mode and receive updates when that changes. This can all be covered cleanly in `crossterm` with no extra deps. That extension seems to be gaining some steam with Ghostty and Kitty now supporting it on the terminal emulator side and neovim on the client side.

Theme config accepts an optional, extended form (like in https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/pull/12098):

```toml
# this is still accepted:
# theme = "ayu_dark"
theme = { dark = "ayu_dark", light = "ayu_light" }
```

On startup we query the current theme mode and subscribe to future changes, swapping when we receive an update.

On the terminal emulator side this needs a bit of setup. The latest Kitty version (v0.38.1) supports this but you also need to follow https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/kittens/themes/#change-color-themes-automatically-when-the-os-switches-between-light-and-dark

This PR needs changes upstream in crossterm - I have a branch https://github.com/the-mikedavis/crossterm/tree/md/theme-mode that I will turn into a PR.

body:
This change replaces all new instances of `java.util.Random` with the marginally slower, but much more secure `java.security.SecureRandom`.

We have to work pretty hard to get computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `java.util.Random` type uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and our changes all look something like this:

```diff
- Random r = new Random();
+ Random r = new java.security.SecureRandom();
```

body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change prevents a file descriptor leak and modernizes the file writing API pattern.

The way the code is written now, the [FileWriter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileWriter.html) never gets closed. Thus, it is up to the garbage collector's objection finalization process to close them at some point. This is not a good practice, and it can lead to a file descriptor leak. In hot code paths, it could cause exhaustion of all the available file descriptors for the system and lead to denial-of-service conditions.

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
-  BufferedWriter writer = new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(f));
+  BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(f.toPath());
```

author: zanieb
body:
Closes #128321

See the issue for context.

There are a few alternative approaches we could take, such as:

- Always including `-lm` during checks (which would over-link)
- Using `PKG_CHECK_MODULES_STATIC` instead of `PKG_CHECK_MODULES` when shared libraries are disabled

I'm not really sure of the trade-offs. This seems like the simplest approach to unblock users who can set `PKG_CONFIG` to include the `--static` flag as mentioned in https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19541#c7

**Addressed issue**
- The "Is module" label is unclear and confusing for users.
- The title in the confirm delete dialog is vague, making it harder for users to understand the action and lead to hesitation or mistakes.

---

**What I have reengineered** 
- **Is module label**
  - The label "Is module" is renamed to "Is extension" across the application to provide better clarity and relevance.
  - Add EntityType.NOTIFICATION_TARGET to the localization files.
- **Title in the confirm delete dialog is vague**
  - Remove the word "Settings"  to improve user understanding in the confirm delete dialog title.

    - **assets**
        -  **all locales files**    
             Remove "Settings" word in the dialog title in en_US.json and remove all outdated localization key in respective language locale file.

#[derive(

body:
## #️⃣ Issue Number

#240 
#241 

## 📝 요약(Summary)

사원등록
- 다음 주소 API 를 연동하여 주소를 정확히 입력할 수 있도록 추가 하였습니다
- 프로필 사진 업로드 시 DB에 없는 사원번호가 자동으로 입력되도록 하였습니다
- 값이 하나라도 입력되지 않을 시 제출할 수 없도록 예외처리 하였습니다

관리자페이지
- 대표 직급은 앞에 관리자 권한이 결재를 처리한 경우의 건 수만 표시할 수 있도록 로직을 수정하였습니다
  - 관리자가 먼저 처리하지 않을 시 대표 직급은 결재 대기건에 대해 카운트가 추가 되지 않습니다

현재 로그인한 정보의 권한을 체크하여 USER 권한일 시 관리자 전용 버튼이 보이지 않도록 하였고
만약 ADMIN 권한일 시 관리자 전용 버튼이 나타나도록 추가하였습니다
 
## 🛠️ PR 유형

어떤 변경 사항이 있나요?

- [x] 새로운 기능 추가
- [ ] 버그 수정
- [ ] CSS 등 사용자 UI 디자인 변경
- [x] 코드에 영향을 주지 않는 변경사항(오타 수정, 탭 사이즈 변경, 변수명 변경)
- [ ] 코드 리팩토링
- [ ] 주석 추가 및 수정
- [ ] 문서 수정
- [ ] 테스트 추가, 테스트 리팩토링
- [ ] 빌드 부분 혹은 패키지 매니저 수정
- [ ] 파일 혹은 폴더명 수정
- [ ] 파일 혹은 폴더 삭제

## 📸스크린샷 (선택)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8ab7870-a598-447b-a93b-b7816ca7b37f)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5473ffbf-0988-4ff0-8671-5c4701dc366f)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/916ccf62-339c-476e-b3d0-4e95a6595497)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41e34478-a684-43b9-951e-40440e154c99)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b4aec3c-a25a-463c-8559-27093bdb8373)
- **대표는 관리자가 먼저 처리한 건이 없다면 결재 대기 카운트가 되지 않습니다**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/247a6fca-3098-4f84-91b4-ade2d63407eb)
- 만약 관리자가 처리된 건이 있다면 카운트가 됩니다
- 관리자 측에서 반려 처리를 한다면 카운트가 되지 않습니다(대표까지 반려할 필요는 없기 때문)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/735ec254-c99a-42dc-a6df-e2dd798d8095)
- 이렇게 대표가 승인 및 반려 해야 하는 건에 대해서만 확인 가능 합니다

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe98bb5e-1cbd-4d60-86b9-8caa2ea84a57)
- 일반 직급은 관리자 전용 버튼이 보이지 않도록 하였습니다

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ae636c4-6434-4947-9700-4e395d70b715)
- 관리자 직급은 관리자 전용 버튼이 보이도록 하였습니다

author: colinbate
body:
## Changes

- Changed the frontmatter parsing in `@astrojs/markdown-remark` to accept TOML format
- Uses `+++` as the delimiters
- Doesn't require configuration
  - If the TOML delimiters are used it will parse as TOML
  - Otherwise defaults to YAML

## Testing

Updated the `frontmatter.test.js` file, adding TOML equivalent tests alongside the existing YAML tests. Worth noting that the TOML test run notably faster, owing to the faster parsing

## Docs

This is certainly something that should be documented. It allows you to use TOML based frontmatter, which is particularly useful if migrating from Hugo or another system that preferred TOML and you don't want to convert potentially thousands of files.

Works for content collections, or with standalone markdown files.

/cc @withastro/maintainers-docs for feedback!

author: mstyura
body:
This will allow pooling of buffers on caller side compared to usage of Vec<u8>.

## Fixes

Lack of possibility to reuse buffers which are consumed by `HttpClient` after request has been sent.

## Design discussion issue
Should old function be kept with deprecated annotation and hence new function had to have a different name or should I just introduce breaking change by changing signature of a function?

## Changes

I propose to change type of body of http request accepted by `HttpClient` trait from `Vec<u8>` to `bytes::Bytes`.
This should unblock pooling of buffers which can be used both for serialization & being http request bodies.
Something like this (pseudo-code to get the idea):
```
async fn export(&mut self, batch: Vec<SpanData>) -> ExportResult  {
    let mut buffer = pool.get();
    let request = self.build_request(&mut buffer, batch);
    let res = send_request(client, request);
    pool.return(buffer);
    res
}
```

author: cincodenada
body:
I ran into memory issues similar to those in #286, notably the `gst_poll_read_control: assertion 'set != NULL' failed` errors.

My first clue was watching `lsof`: neolink continually opened new fd's until it hit a limit (~1024 on my system), at which point it started throwing the assertion errors, so it seemed like there was something opening way too many fd's.

I then did some poking around with `gdb` and `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals` as recommended in [this mailing list](https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/gstreamer-bugs/2017-August/203936.html), which gave me a backtrace for those failed assertions and led me to this code.

I believe this was causing excess memory usage because we were allocating (and keeping permanently in memory, as best I can tell) a pool of pools: for _each unique size of message_, we allocated a new pool of buffers _for that size_, and then held onto it forever.

Which means the memory usage of this pool of pools is a function of the number of **unique message sizes seen** - and at least in my case, judging by some debug logging, the message sizes were essentially random, or at least fairly evenly distributed. Thus, the number of pools we were allocating was functionally unbounded, and we were therefore trying to allocate a _lot_ of permanent pools.

I definitely don't understand the details of what's going on in the rest of the code around this, but this seems like a pretty self-contained change. It seems to me that size-specific buffer pools are intended to be an optimization for the case where you have a small, defined set of common sizes of messages. This does not seem to be the case here: the message sizes, at least in my case, were essentially random.

I thus removed the global pool of pools altogether, and instead simply allocate a new (scoped/limited-lifetime) buffer for every message, which presumably only lives as long as the message.

---

## Project Overview

### **Brief Description**
The **Form Builder Application** allows admins to create dynamic forms with up to 100 questions and various question types (text, checkbox, dropdown). End users can submit responses anonymously, and both users and admins can view analytics for forms and individual questions. The solution is API-driven and built using Django and Django Rest Framework.

---

## Assumptions Made

1. Admins can only access endpoints related to form creation, management, and analytics after authentication.
2. End users are not required to authenticate for form submissions.
3. The public analytics endpoint includes basic question-specific analytics but does not support advanced chart visualization.
4. Form deletion is not implemented as part of the MVP but can be added later.
5. The solution supports up to three question types: text, checkbox, and dropdown.

---

## Testing Credentials

- Admin login credentials (default):
  - **Username:** `admin`
  - **Password:** `admin`
- Token generation endpoint: `/api-token-auth/`

---

## Learning Experience

This project helped me:
1. Deepen my understanding of Django's ORM and RESTful API design principles using DRF.
2. Implement modular code while adhering to DRY and SRP principles for scalability.
3. Explore advanced analytics aggregation techniques for text and choice-based responses.
4. Work with token-based authentication and middleware for secure access control.
5. Enhance skills in writing clear, maintainable, and well-documented APIs.

---

## Time Taken to Complete the Project

Approximately **18–20 hours**, distributed across the following tasks:
1. Designing database models and implementing ORM: 4–5 hours.
2. Developing APIs for form creation, management, and submission: 8 hours.
3. Implementing analytics features: 3 hours.
4. Writing authentication logic and documentation: 3–4 hours.
5. Final testing and cleanup: 1–2 hours.

---

## Potential Enhancements with More Time

1. Implement additional question types (e.g., ranking, date picker, linear scale).
2. Add a user-friendly web-based frontend using Django templates or a modern framework like React.
3. Include detailed analytics visualizations using tools like Chart.js or D3.js.
4. Enhance public analytics endpoints with export options (e.g., CSV, JSON).
5. Optimize database queries for better performance with larger datasets.
6. Implement role-based access control for different admin levels.

body:
Currently, the code generator is written in ESM. On the other hand, the entry point for ts-plugin is written in CJS. Therefore, ts-plugin loads code generator modules via dynamic import.

Dynamic import is an asynchronous API. Therefore, ts-plugin uses `createAsyncLanguageServicePlugin` for initialisation. However, there are some problems with `createAsyncLanguageServicePlugin`.

- https://github.com/volarjs/volar.js/issues/257
- https://github.com/volarjs/volar.js/issues/258

To work around these, we would like to initialise ts-plugin synchronously. So, first of all, we want to make config loading synchronous.

<!--
    Hello! Thanks for submitting a pull request to MusicBrainz Picard. We
    appreciate your time and interest in helping our project!

    Use this template to help us review your change. Not everything is required,
    depending on your change. Keep or delete what is relevant for your change.

    [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/metabrainz/picard/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
-->

# Summary

<!--
    Update the checkbox with an [x] for the type of contribution you are making.
-->

* This is a…
  * [x] Bug fix
  * [ ] Feature addition
  * [ ] Refactoring
  * [ ] Minor / simple change (like a typo)
  * [ ] Other
* **Describe this change in 1-2 sentences**:

# Problem

When saving an ID3 file with LRC synced lyrics, it only accepted a very narrow definition of timestamps (two-digit minutes, two-digit seconds, and three-digit milliseconds). While this is fine for preserving the field (as in PICARD-1092), some plugins may import or download LRCs with different timestamps, and people can edit the field manually and change as well.

No JIRA ticket was open for this problem, and there was no LRC support at all in the previous release.


# Solution

I changed the regular expressions that are used for LRC decoding (`ID3File.__lrc_*_re_parse`), and the corresponding timestamp parsing at `ID3File._parse_lrc_text`. I also added new test cases for the new timestamps.

body:
After noticing a dead link in `page-footer-folge.html` (it appears this was forgotten in dc8fbb07c257e76c0beaa6f36dde376fc8df2e54), I realized there are a few more issues:

* The default footer is in English while episode footers are in German.
* The document language is always German (i.e. `<html lang="de">`).
* Legal links' visual placement looks a bit random.
* It's not clear why there are two different footer variants in the first place. (See caveat below.)

So here's a _proposal_ for an alternative approach. Note that this is merely a _suggestion_ though, a somewhat half-baked one at that; feel free to reject or alter it.

Caveat: Arguably it makes sense for sketchnotes to only be mentioned on episode pages, though the rest should probably be identical? This particular approach just seemed easier from an implementation perspective, avoiding duplication and thus issues like the one that prompted this PR.

## 수정사항

![{9EAF3C7A-CBBB-407F-858E-330DCC63C31D}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3c68c41-211f-416b-a2ad-18134a42a2eb)


- DB Character에 tags 필드 추가

--- 

This pull request includes several changes to the `CharacterDialog` component and the database schema to support tags for characters. The most important changes include adding a new `tags` field to the character schema, updating the form schema and default form values, and creating a new `TagBox` component to handle tag input.

Changes to `CharacterDialog` component:

* Added `tags` field to the form schema in `CharacterDialog.tsx` (`src/components/CharacterDialog.tsx`, [src/components/CharacterDialog.tsxR45](diffhunk://#diff-7e82fff1e79234bde2307c6a47f9103ea296fe02dc9adad874ecfdeb46211e66R45)).
* Updated default form values to include `tags` and `note` fields in `CharacterDialog.tsx` (`src/components/CharacterDialog.tsx`, [src/components/CharacterDialog.tsxR68-R69](diffhunk://#diff-7e82fff1e79234bde2307c6a47f9103ea296fe02dc9adad874ecfdeb46211e66R68-R69)).
* Modified the layout and added `TagBox` component to handle tag input in `CharacterDialog.tsx` (`src/components/CharacterDialog.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7e82fff1e79234bde2307c6a47f9103ea296fe02dc9adad874ecfdeb46211e66L102-R109) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e82fff1e79234bde2307c6a47f9103ea296fe02dc9adad874ecfdeb46211e66L128-R135).

New `TagBox` component:

* Implemented `TagBox` component to manage tag input, including adding and removing tags, and updating the form state in `CharacterDialog.tsx` (`src/components/CharacterDialog.tsx`, [src/components/CharacterDialog.tsxR232-R284](diffhunk://#diff-7e82fff1e79234bde2307c6a47f9103ea296fe02dc9adad874ecfdeb46211e66R232-R284)).

Database schema update:

* Added `tags` field to the `Character` interface and updated the database schema to include `tags` in `db.ts` (`src/lib/db.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-196dc6cfdb581213173439841d9e85ada909cf40face80a3ac1b6739bbd85bf6R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-196dc6cfdb581213173439841d9e85ada909cf40face80a3ac1b6739bbd85bf6L49-R50).

<!--
  make this PR easy to find:

  - assign: yourself

-->

## Behavior

### Files

- [ ] The file name describes the function's behavior
- [ ] There is a module docstring in the function file
- [ ] The test file's name matches the function file name -
  `/tests/test_file_name.py`
- [ ] There is a module docstring in the tests file

### Unit Tests

- [ ] The test class has a helpful name in PascalCase
- [ ] The test class has a docstring
- Every unit test has
  - [ ] A helpful name
  - [ ] A clear docstring
  - [ ] Only one assertion
  - [ ] There is no logic in the unit test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] There are tests for defensive assertions
- [ ] There are tests for boundary cases

### Function Docstring

- [ ] The function's behavior is described
- The function's arguments are described:
  - [ ] Type
  - [ ] Purpose
  - [ ] Other assumptions (eg. if it's a number, what's the expected range?)
- The return value is described
  - [ ] Type
  - [ ] Other assumptions are documented
- The defensive assertions are documented using `Raises:`
  - [ ] Each assumption about an argument is checked with an assertion
  - [ ] Each assertion checks for _only one_ assumption about the argument
- [ ] Include 3 or more (passing!) doctests

### The Function

- [ ] The function's name describes it's behavior
- [ ] The function's name matches the file name
- [ ] The function has correct type annotations

## Strategy

### Do's

- [ ] Variable names help to understand the strategy
- [ ] Any comments are clear and describe the strategy
- [ ] Lines of code are spaced to help show different stages of the strategy

### Don'ts

- [ ] The function's strategy _is not_ described in the documentation
- [ ] Comments explain the _strategy_, **not** the _implementation_
- [ ] The function _does not_ have more comments than code
  - If it does, consider finding a new strategy or a simpler implementation

## Implementation

- [ ] The code passes the formatting checks
- [ ] The code passes all Ruff linting checks
- [ ] The code has no (reasonable) Pylint errors
  - In code review, you can decide when fixing a Pylint error is helpful and
    when it's too restricting.
- [ ] Variables are named with snake_case
- [ ] Variable names are clear and helpful
- [ ] The code follows the strategy as simply as possible
- [ ] The implementation is as simple as possible given the strategy
- [ ] The code includes defensive assertions
- [ ] Defensive assertions include as little logic as possible

body:
Follow-up of #99986.
*Note : This PR is ready for review, but kept in Draft state on purpose until dependencies get resolved.*

### Outline
**This PR enables rendering and editing arbitrary large scenes and objects in the Editor**.

This is especially useful for open worlds, space scenes and alike.

This is achieved by raising the maximum allowed far (and near) distance in the editor's View settings, and fixing a handful of numerical precision issues :
- Move computations happening in world space to view space for :
  - Gizmo positionning
  - Gizmo handles picking
  - Objects picking
- Fix box select of very far away objects
- Fix orthogonal camera positionning with very large zfar

### Dependencies
- #99986 (enables large zfar rendering)
- #100511 (remove numerical precision issues on raycast functions)
- #100478 (remove numerical precision issue on gizmo picking)
- #100718 (enables view space raycasting)

### Demo
[large_zfar_editor.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18269271/large_zfar_editor.zip)

Vegetation is ~1m tall and ~10m from the origin
The terrain is 10 km large
The earth's radius is 6,000 km
The moon's radius is 1,700 km and is 400,000 km from the origin
The sun's radius is 700,000 km and is 150 million km from the origin
The Andromeda galaxy is 152,000 light-years wide and is 2.5 million light years from the observer

[output.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/319b49c5-d737-48f0-af93-1e4b74f2dfac)

- *Bugsquad edit: This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15086.*

body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The test relied on a 100ms sleep to ensure that controller was done.  If that race was lost, one goroutine was intentionally prevented from completing by locking a mutex permanently. A TODO was left about detecting that.

Adding goroutine leak checking in
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126387 revealed that this race indeed sometimes is lost because the goroutine
leaked (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129400).

Waiting for controller shutdown instead of relying on timing should fix this.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #129400

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I could not reproduce the flake locally, but this should fix it.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

This PR introduces pagination support for the GET /progreses API, aimed at improving the performance and scalability when dealing with large datasets. The feature is currently gated behind a development flag for testing. By default, the size is set to 100 items per page.

size: The number of items per page. The size can be a value between 1 and 100. If not specified, it defaults to 100.

Included prev and next links in the response to allow easy navigation between pages:

This pull request includes changes to enhance the Server-Sent Events (SSE) handler in `src/server/sse-server.ts`. The updates focus on improving the flexibility and functionality of the SSE callback and adding guidance for handling long-running operations.

Enhancements to SSE handler:

* [`src/server/sse-server.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-fa708660b9c7234bcebe2b24466ffd7d85c5bc90d0576b08cce84d9b960e4141L36-R37): Updated the `SSECallback` type to allow the callback to return a promise that resolves to a cleanup function or a function that returns a promise.
* [`src/server/sse-server.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-fa708660b9c7234bcebe2b24466ffd7d85c5bc90d0576b08cce84d9b960e4141R47-R60): Added a hint in the documentation to avoid awaiting long-running operations directly in the callback to prevent blocking the initial response.
* [`src/server/sse-server.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-fa708660b9c7234bcebe2b24466ffd7d85c5bc90d0576b08cce84d9b960e4141L66-R80): Modified the `start` method in `createSSEHandler` to be asynchronous, allowing for better handling of asynchronous operations within the callback.
* [`src/server/sse-server.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-fa708660b9c7234bcebe2b24466ffd7d85c5bc90d0576b08cce84d9b960e4141L89-R103): Updated the invocation of the `callback` in `createSSEHandler` to await its result, ensuring proper handling of asynchronous callbacks.

body:
This pull request introduces the implementation of the following features:

JWT Token Manipulation:
Token Storage and Management: The app now securely handles JWT tokens by storing access tokens, refresh tokens, and event tokens using a custom TokenManager class.
Token Decoding and Validation: A new JwtService class was introduced to decode JWT tokens and validate their integrity. This includes functionality to check the token’s validity, extract user roles (Admin, EO, SP, etc.), and handle token expiration.
Login and Logout: The login process was updated to handle JWT-based authentication, including setting access and refresh tokens upon successful login. The logout function clears all tokens from local storage.
User Registration for EO and SP:
Event Organizer (EO) Registration: A new registration flow was added for EO users, including fields like name, surname, email, phoneNumber, and an addressDTO object. The backend responds with the user details and JWT tokens for the authenticated user.
Service Provider (SP) Registration: Similar to EO registration, SP users can register with additional details like company, description, and photos. This feature also includes token management upon successful registration.
Login/Logout Implementation:
Login Flow: The app now uses the JWT authentication mechanism for logging in. After a successful login, the access and refresh tokens are stored using TokenManager, and the user is redirected to the Home screen.
Logout Flow: The user can log out, clearing stored tokens, effectively ending the session. The logout functionality is added for user security and access control.
Detailed Changes:
JWT Service Implementation:

Created a JwtService class to manage JWT token decoding, validation, and expiration checks.
Added utility functions to decode tokens, extract user roles (isAdmin(), isEo(), isSp()), and retrieve user information such as id and email from the JWT.
TokenManager Class:

A TokenManager class was implemented to store and retrieve the access token, refresh token, and event token, providing a central management system for all tokens.
Methods include setToken(), getToken(), and clearTokens() for managing token lifecycle.
Register EO and SP Flow:

Introduced two new DTOs for the registration of EO and SP, RegisterEoRequestDTO and RegisterSpRequestDTO, including all necessary user details.
Backend integration to send these requests and receive appropriate responses containing JWT tokens.
On successful registration, the server responds with user details and the tokens which are then stored for future use.
Login Flow:

Login function now sends a POST request with the user credentials and stores the received JWT tokens upon a successful response.
The LoginActivity handles UI updates and user redirection to the Home screen after login.
Logout Flow:

Implemented logout functionality that removes all stored tokens from the TokenManager.
Testing:
Unit Tests: Unit tests were written for the JwtService to verify token decoding, validation, and role extraction.
Manual Testing: The login and registration flows were manually tested for both EO and SP users, ensuring that tokens are correctly handled and user data is properly saved.
Edge Cases: Handled edge cases such as invalid tokens, failed login attempts, and expired tokens.
Potential Issues or Areas for Review:
Token Expiration Handling: The token expiration handling logic is currently based on decoding the token and comparing the expiration time with the current time. Ensure that this logic is aligned with the backend’s token expiration strategy.
Error Handling in Auth Flows: Error messages from the server during login/registration are currently logged but not displayed to the user. A UI message or toast notification can be added for better user feedback.
Next Steps:
UI Enhancements: Improve the user interface for login and registration screens to handle token expiration, showing error messages, and providing visual feedback on login status.
Role-Based UI Updates: Implement additional UI components that adapt based on the user’s role (e.g., Admin, EO, SP).
Refresh Token Logic: Implement refresh token functionality to handle token expiration more gracefully.

author: realjoshbyrnes
body:
Currently the regex when a country code and phone number are provided matches invalid sequences, and doesn't match numbers where leading zeroes are provided.

eg. Consider the Australian Number (02) 5550 1234

A VoIP provider may send one of the following three phone number formats, which are all valid:
* \+ 61 2 5550 1234
* 61 2 5550 1234
* 02 5550 1234

Currently, the default regular expression that FusionPBX provides would allow you to match one (format with 61) or the other (format with leading 0). Users have stated on the forums that they have created both entries for each number.

The default regular expression would also match +255501234 (a Tanzania phone number in this case, but could be anywhere in the world depending on the number).

The new regex ensures that the optional plus is only present before the country code, and also allows the matching of a preceding zero.

Caveat: The new regex, while not matching arbitrary numbers like the old one, does match where a leading zero should not be used (eg. North America).

author: veracity0
body:
Modern shop.php NPC stores use ShopRow objects.
Multiple ShopRows can provide the same item, using different ingredients.

This PR has three examples:

1) Kiwi Kwiki Mart can sell a mini kiwitini by mixing a mini kiwi with either a bottle of gin or a bottle of vodka
2) Grandma Sea Monkey can provide a crappy Mer-Kin mask by degrading either an existing Mer-kin scholar mask or Mer-kin gladiator mask, or make a new one with an aerated diving helmet
3) The Primordial Soup Kitchen sells 3 basic soups for Chroner, but can combine any of those soups with five different kinds of protogenetic chunklets to make fancier soups; three recipes each for five soups.

KoLmafia has three ways to model ShopRow shops:

1) A mixing method, using concoctions.txt, Concoction.java,  ConcoctionDatabase.java, and a CreateItemRequest subclass
2) A Coinmaster, using coinmasters.txt and a CoinMasterRequest subclass, with the usual hooks in other files.
*** The same item can appear in multiple shops. Boris's key in both the Vending Machine and Cosmic Ray's Bazaar.
*** The same item can appear multiple times with different recipes. Primordial Soup Kitchen.
3) An NPCPurchaseRequest using npcstores.txt, for Meat-only shops.
*** The same item can appear in multiple shops. Bugbear Bakery, and Madeline's Baking Supply are identical, and overlap with Degrassi Knoll Bakery and Hardware Store

-> A shop can have some items for sale for Meat and others for items. I.e., can be both an NPC store and a coinmaster.
The Armory and Leggery has stuff for Meat and also Standard Rewards from previous years for pulverized equipment.
-> A shop can have the SAME item available for either Meat or an item.
The Black Market has the Red Zeppelin Ticket either for Meat or a priceless diamond

For such stores, we have entries in both npcstores.txt and coinmasters.txt

Ways to access shops:

1) The MallSearch frame shows PurchaseRequests for user stores, NPC stores, and Coinmasters
*** NPCStoreDatabase uses HashMultimaps indexed by itemId.
--> We display the first that is available to you. Should we display all of them? Probably yes.
*** CoinmastersDatabase uses a HashMap indexed by item and stores only the last-registered PurchaseRequest.
--> We should use a HashMultimap and display all of them. *** DONE

2) The CoinmastersFrame displays lists of AdventureResults (from buyItems or sellItems) or ShopRows (from shopRows). The former does not allow multiple ways to buy the same item, but the latter does.
--> Any Coinmaster that has multiple recipes must use ShopRows.
Is is easy to convert from buyItems and sellItems to using those.
--> Are there any existing coinmasters we should convert?
The Primordial Soup Kitchen *** DONE
Kiwi Kwiki Mart *** DONE
Grandma Sea Monkey -  currently a mixing method. Should we make it a Coinmaster?
Elf Guard Armory - implemented as sell items  and it is obsolete
Crimbuccaneer Junkworks - ditto
Crimbo 2014 - ditto

3) "acquire" will look for items by itemId and is willing to purchase from a mall store, an NPC store, or to "create" it, using a mixing method or coinmaster.
Creating is done via a CreateItemRequest.getInstance(itemId), for which there is one available for every concoction.
Every mixing method registers Concoctions for everything it can create.
Every Coinmaster purchase request registers a Concoction that uses it.
*** If a mixing method can create the same item in multiple ways, only the last is stored.
*** If a coinmaster registers purchase requests, only the last one is stored in a concoction.
*** If multiple coinmasters register purchase requests, only the last is stored in a concoction.
--> See Boris's key. You can "acquire Boris's Key" and it will try to go to the Vending Machine, since that was the last-register coinmaster purchase request.
*** Suppose we register multiple concoctions, what will CreateItemRequest.getInstance(itemId) do?

4) The Usables section of the ItemManager displays list of Concoctions.
That is filled from ConcoctionPool.concoctions().
ConcoctionPool uses a HashMap from itemId to Concoction.
*** Only one recipe is associated with a concoction; the mini kiwitini will be made with vodka, not gin
*** If we want multiple concoctions for the same itemId, need a HashMultimap.

I see work in the following areas:

1) CoinmasterDatabase needs to register multiple purchase requests for the same item. *** DONE
2) MallPurchaseFrame needs to display all CoinMasterPurchaseRequests. *** DONE
3) ConcoctionPool needs to register multiple concoctions for the same item.
4) ConcoctionDatabase's "usable" lists need to store all concoctions for the same item.
5) CreateItemRequest.getInstance(itemId) needs to find a usable creation method.
6) Since it is clear that row numbers are unique, duplicate detection should go in ShopRowDatabase

Issues:

A shop can be enabled or disabled, with a reason ("you have to find Grandma Sea Monkey first")
-> mixing methods handle that with a flag in concoctions.txt (MANUAL) for individual items
-> NPC stores are available or not via code.
-> coinmasters can be generally available or not - in code - using accessible() method
*** How do we disable individual items?

Mixing methods (as subclasses of CreateItemRequest) will - if so coded - super.makeIngredients(), which will create or buy whatever you need.
*** Coinmaster classes have no such paradigm.
--> Should they? Should CoinMasterRequest provide a makeIngredients() method of some sort?

This is a Draft, for now. I've put in a lot of work, but no ETA on completion, yet.

Done so far:

1) CoinmasterData provides a Manual method, in which a subclass can designate certain rows to NOT register a PurchaseRequest and a Concoction
2) test_shop_grandma.html shows all of her items, although some of them only show with certan ingredients in inventory
3) I added the three shops to coinmasters.txt. Until/unless a CoinmasterData subclass is created to support them - and the existing CreateItemRequest subclass for the mixing method is removed, there is no visible effect for this.
4) I added The Primordial Soup Kitchen as a coinmaster.
5) Detect errors in coinmaster parsing:
- blank cost ended up as a null
- duplicate rows can get added.
6) Create ShopsDatabase and shops.php to document all known shop.php "whichshop" shop ids
7) Improve title of Primorial Soup Kitchen in the CoinmastersFrame by abbrviating the names of the currencies.
8) Coinmasters can register multiple PurchaseRequests for the same item. The MallSearchFrame gets all of them and add all of them. Therefore "lip soup" will list all three possible recipes.
9) I made Kiwi Kwiki Mart a coinmaster, rather than a mixing method.
One effect of this is that ConcoctionsDatabase will not include it without autoSatisfyWithCoinmasters.
This will be an active Coinmaster for testing multiple Concoctions in the ItemManager's Usables lists.
10) Added "test row-duplicate-items" which detects rows with identical items and prints them all to the session log.

body:
## Summary:
This PR builds upon the previous update to the merchant contract management system ( #17 ), introducing two key improvements:
1. Enhanced sharing functionality for merchant contract links.
2. A refined notification system for link sharing and copying actions.

---

## Changes Overview:
### Code Modifications:
1. **`package.json`**:
   - Updated dependencies to include enhancements for sharing and clipboard functionality.

2. **`page.tsx`**:
   - Updated page title to better reflect editing functionality (`"Edit Merchant Contract | Details"`).

3. **`form.tsx`**:
   - Improved error handling logic for better user feedback when submitting forms.

4. **`merchantDetailsForm.tsx`**:
   - Added a **"Share"** button for mobile platforms using the `RWebShare` library.
   - Created a new notification component (`LinkNotification`) to indicate whether the link was "Copied" or "Shared."
   - Enhanced modal messaging to guide users on sharing or copying the link.

5. **`successState.tsx`**:
   - Updated the success modal to include an `extraComponent` prop, allowing the addition of buttons for actions like sharing or copying links.

---

## Key Features:
1. **Improved Sharing Functionality**:
   - Added platform-specific sharing logic using `RWebShare`.
   - For platforms without native sharing support, a "Copy Link" button is provided as a fallback.

2. **Refined Notifications**:
   - Introduced a notification bar to inform users when a link is successfully "Copied" or "Shared."
   - Notifications automatically disappear after a few seconds.

3. **Enhanced User Experience**:
   - Updated UI components to provide clearer instructions and feedback to users.

---

## User Impact:
1. Sales team members can now share contract links directly via native sharing tools on mobile devices.
2. Notifications provide real-time feedback, improving user confidence in actions like copying or sharing links.
3. The updated success modal ensures users are well-informed about the next steps.

## Automatic deployments with Hydrogen and Oxygen

This pull request adds a workflow file that enables GitHub to [automatically deploy](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/deployments) your [Hydrogen](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen) app each time you push or merge changes.

Pushes to your `main` branch deploy to your [production environment](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/environments). Pushes to any other branch deploy to your preview environment:

Git branch | Environment | URL
--- | --- | ---
`main` | Production | https://arthur-f227dfcd20b8c1e47f4b.o2.myshopify.dev
(All other branches) | Preview | {hash}.myshopify.dev

You can also create your own [custom environments](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/environments#managing-environments) (like "Staging" or "QA") and assign them to your own [custom domains](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/migrate/redirect-traffic#step-1-set-up-the-domains).

## Developing locally 💻

After you’ve cloned your project, install the dependencies and run the local development server:

```sh
npm install && npm run dev
```

Link your local development environment to your Shopify store to render your product inventory data:

```sh
npx shopify hydrogen link --storefront "Arthur"
```

[Linking your project](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#link) automatically keeps your local environment variables in sync with Oxygen, allows you to query your store data, and lets you [create deployments](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#deploy) from the command line at any time. Check the complete list of [Hydrogen CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli) for a complete list of features.

author: pmarkaide
body:
Sync event from 42 to Gcal **only if the event is updated**. Ignore already up-to-date events.

This patch adds an SQLite database with an events TABLE and minimal fields ( 42 ID, GCal ID, title, begin_at, last_updated) that store the relation between both event type IDs and the updated time. The initialization function now calls the previously developed `deleteAllEvents` and `fetchAllCampusEvents` but now it also initializes the db and populates it with the events data.

After this, the main `syncEvents` function will call `fetchUpdatedCampusEvents` and will compare the update time of these events with the database. Based on this will `POST` a new event, `PUT` an updated event or do nothing. These changes make the number of calls minimal.

body:
<!-- Write **BELOW** The Headers and **ABOVE** The comments else it may not be viewable. -->
<!-- You can view Contributing.MD for a detailed description of the pull request process. -->

## About The Pull Request

<!-- Describe The Pull Request. Please be sure every change is documented or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR! -->

Makes disablers bulky. Made mostly due to [this PR](https://github.com/BeeStation/BeeStation-Hornet/pull/11858) that reduces disablers shot count

## Why It's Good For The Game

<!-- Please add a short description of why you think these changes would benefit the game. If you can't justify it in words, it might not be worth adding.
-->

To put it as simple as can be, disabler does two incompatible things at once. It acts as a primary weapon for security, by being a 4 shot stam crit with a massive energy pool, while also being a sidearm that can be used in tandem with other weapons like shotguns by being stored in the backpack. In isolation either of these are acceptable, but when combined they are problematic. 

Think about it objectively. If today someone were to try to add a weapon to security that they can carry at any alert level, keep concealed in a bag, that only requires 4 shots to stamcrit, that has enough energy to stamcrit 6 people, they would be laughed out of the room.

You might ask why the size and not the ammo count or the damage? The answer is precedent. The damage and ammo count are not insane compared to other weapons, it's roughly equivalent to existing e-guns. The size is not. The only comparable weapons are the X-01 and the service pistols, both of which are head of staff exclusive items.

The problem with disablers being large items is that it encourages security to keep two primary weapons on them. When you offer this opportunity, players jump at it for obvious reasons. Look no further than the tonfa. It was proposed as an **alternative** to the baton, but instead of being an alternative it is used in _addition_ to the baton. You can keep a tonfa and a baton in your sec belt, so why not do it? It's not the players fault for taking the obviously superior path. Just the same, armory weapons are not an alternative to disablers they are an addition to them. You can freely load yourself up with all the lethal weaponry you want knowing that since your disabler fits in your bag, you're prepared for any situation that you have to take someone in non-lethally. God forbid someone realizes you can dual wield disablers.

Isn't being able to deal with threats lethally and non-lethally a good thing? Yes! That's why energy guns and non-lethal ballistics ammo exist! Use those!
 
This is getting rather long so I'll cut it short here, I'm willing to throw verbal fisticuffs with anyone about this. If people really don't like disablers being bulky I can go with idea #2 where their damage and shot count is reduced, but size is preserved, leaning into the sidearm rather than primary weapon classification.

TLDR: Disablers being large instead of bulky is outside the norm and encourages unsportsmanlike conduct

author: andiwand
body:
Adds data paths from poppler, fontconfig and pdf2htmlex to `HtmlConfig`. This seems a bit odd but I believe it is ultimately the best choice. We decided to use a single config struct to steer all html translations. This makes the interface way easier and more generic. Since data paths are generally only known at runtime (Android/iOS) we have to communicate them somehow. Previously this was done via environment variables but I think it is more generic to use C++ and to put it directly into the `HtmlConfig` as it ultimately configures the HTML translation.

The paths known at compile time are defaulted into these new config params. Note that these default paths will not be meaningful for some platforms and we might even want to hide them from the binary.

author: andrewshkrob
body:
AA loses location info when the device is locked and OM is not launched.
We already had this issue and this is the only way I know to resolve it.

AA will find the location again during the navigation because it starts NavigationService which has location type.
But during the free drive AA can't fetch location.

The reason why we removed it is that we can't ensure the user has granted location permission before starting the AA app.
And if the service doesn't have specific permissions for its type it will crash within a time limit (5-15s I guess).

It's been almost a year since I reported this issue to Google and still no response. https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/322622698
https://github.com/organicmaps/organicmaps/pull/8860

I think it's better to have some low-chance fails (when the user installs the app and immediately launches it in AA without starting it on the phone first) instead of a constant non-working location.

To summarize:
Without the fix: no location when the app is running only on AA
With the fix: the app may crash for the users (with Android 14) who started the app on AA without granting location permissions before (from the app on the phone)

author: alufolie91
body:
Basically replaces the spectator camera with what was the demo camera

This fixes numerous issues with the spectator camera like:
- you now can pass through walls, floors and ceilings. no more getting stuck on certain maps and you can explore freely!
- when speccing midgame your camera now wont get put at the map start anymore but instead remains where you were
- this also allowed to add a freecam toggle so you can just freely control your camera while INGAME (useful for screenshots that should include you)

also Camera float and sink button are now rebindable
and the postimg stuff has been moved to the camera struct, since its a visual thing relieng on the camera anyways, this just makes more sense

ontop of this, this "clientside" fixes some spectator desynchs;
essentially, the old spectatormovement occasionally causes desynchs, with this, it is blocked by not building any control cmds while in freecam/spectator state, since those are uneeded.
Sadly this does not fix desynchs by vanilla /older saturn/ other custom clients

author: chandonpierre
body:
This reverts commit 9cd01352c3caa569010f085be2010aa04f19c4ca.

This seems to cause more problems than it solves - 

```
< X-Docker-Registry-Proxy-Cache-Upstream-Status: HIT
< X-Docker-Registry-Proxy-Cache-Type: manifest-secondary
< Accept-Ranges: bytes
< 
* transfer closed with 1609 bytes remaining to read
* Closing connection 0
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, close notify (256):
curl: (18) transfer closed with 1609 bytes remaining to read
```

Since cache key is defined in common, slice module applies to manifests as well, which seems to lead to `unexpected EOF` pulling image manifests on occasion

This PR adds cloud integration for SensorPush devices. It communicates with the publicly available [Cloud API](https://www.sensorpush.com/gateway-cloud-api) using the [sensorpush-api](https://pypi.org/project/sensorpush-api/) and [sensorpush-ha](https://pypi.org/project/sensorpush-ha/) Python packages. Care was taken to ensure that presented devices appeared the same as those created by the existing SensorPush integration. A [G1 WiFi Gateway](https://www.sensorpush.com/products/p/g1-gateway) is required to make use of the Cloud API.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR is a re-submission of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/121890, which fixes several issues reported by reviewers. I would like to send a heartfelt apology to @joostlek, @edenhaus, and @frenck - I was caught between dueling schedules and I wasn't able to do the work needed to get it over the finish line. I was finally able to put in the time over the holiday break to make requested changes in addition to improved unit tests, strict typing, async dependencies, and websession injection (whew!)

author: adriennebosch
body:
### Summary
This pull request introduces a comprehensive cleanup and enhancement of the project codebase, focusing on improving maintainability, robustness, and modularity. Key changes include better error handling, centralized service configuration, enhanced logging, and improved separation of concerns.

---

### Key Changes

#### General Code Cleanup
- Removed redundant code comments.
- Eliminated redundant logging.
- Adjusted startup location of windows and window sizes.
- Updated methods to use dependency injection (DI) for accessing logger instances where applicable.

#### Exception Handling
- Added robust exception handling in the `OnStartup` method to log errors during application startup.
- Enhanced defensive coding in `HotkeyService` to provide meaningful exceptions for invalid window handles.

#### Resource Management
- Ensured proper disposal of `IHotkeyService` in the `OnExit` method.
- Added `Dispose` and `Initialize` methods to the `IHotkeyService` interface to align with its implementation.

#### Centralized Service Configuration
- Centralized service initialization logic in the `ConfigureServices` method for improved maintainability.

#### Thread Safety and Lifecycle Management
- Improved thread safety and UI thread access in `HotkeyService`.
- Delayed `HotkeyService` initialization until `MainWindow` is fully loaded to avoid lifecycle timing issues.
- Introduced `WindowInteropService` to decouple `HotkeyService` from direct `Window` lifecycle management.
- Updated `StartupManager` to subscribe to `MainWindow.Loaded` event for proper `HotkeyService` initialization.

#### Hotkey Management
- Refactored `HotkeyManager` to align with the updated `HotkeyService` interface and lifecycle management logic.
- Created `Infrastructure.Constants.ModifierKeys` to define modifier keys, enhancing code clarity and reducing duplication.

#### Logging Enhancements
- Updated logging configurations to include the source class or type in logs.
- Standardized `MessageBox` titles in `HotkeyService` and `TTSService` using constants for consistency.

#### Clipboard Handling
- Updated `GetClipboardText` to return a nullable string, improving clarity when the function fails.

#### Settings Management
- Removed unnecessary saving of settings on each UI settings change, improving performance.
- Updated `SettingsService` to use DI for accessing the logger and displaying messages through `MessageService`.

#### User Interaction
- Introduced `DissonanceMessageBox` and `DissonanceMessageBoxViewModel` for user message display.
- Added `MessageService` and `IMessageService` for handling message interactions.
- Updated `HotkeyService`, `TTSService`, and `SettingsService` to use `MessageService` for displaying user messages.

---

### Detailed List of Changes

#### Services and Infrastructure
- **`ClipboardService`**: Access logger instance through DI.
- **`HotkeyService`**:
  - Access logger instance through DI.
  - Use `MessageService` for displaying messages.
  - Add defensive error handling and lifecycle management improvements.
- **`TTSService`**:
  - Use DI for logger access.
  - Utilize `MessageService` for user notifications.
- **`SettingsService`**:
  - Use DI for logger access.
  - Refactor to display messages via `MessageService`.

#### New Features
- Added `WindowInteropService` for decoupling `Window` lifecycle dependencies.
- Added `DissonanceMessageBox` and `DissonanceMessageBoxViewModel` for user notifications.
- Introduced `MessageService` for centralized message handling.

#### Modularity and Separation of Concerns
- Improved lifecycle management for `HotkeyService` through event-driven initialization.
- Refactored code for better modularity in application lifecycle and hotkey management.

---

body: This Clarity smart contract manages digital credentials on the Stacks blockchain. It allows authorized institutions to issue, verify, and revoke digital credentials (like diplomas or certificates). The contract maintains two main data structures: one for verified credential issuers and another for the credentials themselves. Each credential includes details like recipient, issuer, type, issue date, expiry date, and a hash of the credential data. The contract implements security features such as input validation, authorization checks, and expiration enforcement. Only registered and active issuers can issue credentials, and only the original issuer can revoke them. The contract owner manages issuer registration and suspension.

## Summary

Before the new username system was implemented, the defaut_avatar index used depended on the discriminator. By introducing the new username system, discriminators were all set to "0", and the index is now dependent on the user ID, but users still on the old system would keep using the index provided by their discriminator. (see https://discord.com/developers/docs/reference#image-formatting-cdn-endpoints)
This behaviour wasn't implemented correctly in nextcord : the condition for checking if a user is using the new username system was done in reverse, resulting in differences from the official client.
This PR aims to fix that.

body:
This has two advantages :
- Trades buffer update performance (constant time per frame) for geometry culling performance (linear time with the number of objects). Considering Occlusion Culling is primarily designed for large scenes, this should have a small positive impact
- Removes the need for calling `length()` on the geometry position vector (Z coordinate is used instead) which avoids overflows with very far away objects (> ~1e19m in single precision) and makes Occlusion Culling suitable for large scenes

This may also allow removing orthogonal vs perspective code paths during culling (to be investigated)

This pull request introduces several new features and improvements to the booking and user modules, including new endpoints, service type integration, and enhanced user properties.

### New Endpoints and Features:

* Added a new endpoint to `BookingController` to get all booking services filtered by `serviceTypeId` with pagination, sorting, and status filter. (`src/modules/booking/booking.controller.ts`)
* Added a new endpoint to `UserManagerController` to get the count of staff, including total, receptionist, and service staff counts. (`src/modules/user/userManager.controller.ts`)

### Service Type Integration:

* Integrated `ServiceTypeModule` and `ServiceTypeService` into the booking module to support the new endpoint and service type filtering. (`src/modules/booking/booking.module.ts`, `src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d662c788f1edf885cb06da01dc60f7651479c0df347eaa06680864c7fd8d8a8aR12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d662c788f1edf885cb06da01dc60f7651479c0df347eaa06680864c7fd8d8a8aR23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b5a7938ee79396bd5d2b13a7daacdf1ea5facaab73b95c0b4dfd044004c2a5c1R1) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b5a7938ee79396bd5d2b13a7daacdf1ea5facaab73b95c0b4dfd044004c2a5c1R44) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b5a7938ee79396bd5d2b13a7daacdf1ea5facaab73b95c0b4dfd044004c2a5c1L472-R481) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b5a7938ee79396bd5d2b13a7daacdf1ea5facaab73b95c0b4dfd044004c2a5c1R546-R638)

### Enhanced User Properties:

* Updated `UpdateUserRequestDTO` to include `ApiProperty` decorators for better Swagger documentation. (`src/modules/user/dto/request/updateUser.request.dto.ts`)
* Modified `UserService` to return `serviceTypeId` as a string if it exists. (`src/modules/user/user.service.ts`)

### Additional Improvements:

* Added role-based access control to the `findOne` method in `UserController`. (`src/modules/user/user.controller.ts`)
* Included `ApiResponse` import in `UserManagerController` for better response documentation. (`src/modules/user/userManager.controller.ts`)

These changes enhance the functionality and documentation of the booking and user modules, providing better filtering, sorting, and user management capabilities.

author: christhrasher
body:
## Description

While [upgrading SFGUI to SFML 3](https://github.com/TankOs/SFGUI/compare/master...ChrisThrasher:SFGUI:feature/sfml-three) I found a number of places where event data is being modified. This caused some problems because `sf::Event` currently provides on easy way to modify the event short of creating a brand new `Event` object then using `operator=` to assign it to the initial event. The `sf::Event` class is just some data with a type-safe interface. I see no reason to prevent easy modification of the underlying data. Most users will never need this, but for some more advanced use cases it will come in handy.

author: timonz1535
body:
#3014

Technical changes:
- **luadoc Parser** now considers `.` and `*` as **Symbol** because I want to parse these tokens after **code** block, otherwise they just disappeared:
```
`T`.Name
code symbol name
`T`*
code symbol
```
- **parseCodePattern** now checks these symbols `.*-` and integer as part of the name but only after **code** block.
- Fixed crash when tokens >= 8 because it was `for i = 2, 8 do` and **finishOffset** remained `nil`.
- Fixed crash with double **code** "\`T\`\`T\`" because of `content ~= nextContent` when `暂时不支持多generic` then we call `("%s%s"):format(val)` and 2nd argument was expected.
- Fixed wrong **getStart** `start` tokens of returned result.
- **parseCode** was replaced with **parseCodePattern** because it didn't allow to process the cases "\`T\`Name" or "\`T\`*", now they are merged.
- Added simple tests.

author: eldritchcarmaker
body:
This system is more expandable, gives more examples to users looking to use the system themselves, and you should always use your own API

### Changes made in this pull request
Nautilus previously used its own file IO for various configuration options, this did nothing but obscure the codebase and have repeated code in multiple places, especially as they didn't all use the same system. I've left this intact for the various caches (craft tree cache, equipment type cache, techtype cache, etc) as these are not "configuration" options per-se but I wouldn't be against moving these into the configuration system as well for consolidation (or another consolidated json system, distinct from the config) I have also left the heading_states file alone, for the same reason, although I would also consider merging that into the config

### Breaking changes
Should be none, so long as the change works and mods don't do anything stupid by trying to mess with the config themselves

### Tested in subnautica, not below zero
Changes should be internal enough to not matter, but it still needs to get rudimentary bz testing. Testing in sn1 could also be more extensive, especially regarding the "Enable mod databank entries" option as I truly have no idea what it's meant to do

# Before merging
Test in BZ, and look over the "Enable mod databank entries" because it currently does literally nothing. If it has a use, let me know what it is and write up a tooltip for it. If it doesn't, we need to remove it instead. From a cursory glance at it before this overhaul, it didn't do anything in the past either.
