author: cmenders
body:
------This PR has been replicated in #160--------------------------------------------------------
This PR introduces an Interactive Mode to our Chat Workflow, enabling step-by-step execution of workflow phases. When Interactive Mode is enabled, the workflow pauses at each iteration until a “next” signal is received from the user (via button on interface). This allows for incremental review or user input before continuing the workflow to subsequent phases.

### Asynchronous Phase Execution

ChatPhase.run_phase() has been converted to async def.
Inside the phase loop (i.e., each iteration), if phase_config.interactive is True, the phase now waits on an asyncio.Event for the “next” signal.
Example snippet:
```python
if self.phase_config.interactive:
    logger.info("Waiting for 'next' signal ...")
    self.workflow.next_iteration_event.clear()  # So we don’t auto-proceed
    await self.workflow.next_iteration_event.wait()  # Block until signaled
```

Async Workflow Flow

BaseWorkflow.run_phases() is now async def run_phases(self) and uses await phase.run_phase().
BaseWorkflow.run() is also converted to async def, and it iterates through the async generator returned by run_phases().
In server.py, any code that calls workflow.run() (e.g. run_workflow) now does await workflow.run() instead of calling it synchronously. This ensures the application does not block the event loop while waiting for user signals.
next_iteration_event in Workflow

When a ChatWorkflow is created with interactive=True, we set up an asyncio.Event called next_iteration_event.
At the beginning of each phase iteration, if Interactive Mode is on, the code awaits this event before proceeding to the next iteration.
An additional HTTP endpoint (/workflow/next/{workflow_id}) is introduced to trigger workflow.next_iteration_event.set(), unblocking the workflow.
New HTTP Endpoint

In server.py, we add an endpoint for the user to signal the next iteration:
```python
@app.post("/workflow/next/{workflow_id}")
async def signal_next_iteration(workflow_id: str):
    workflow_data = active_workflows.get(workflow_id)
    if not workflow_data:
        return {"error": "Workflow not found"}

    workflow = workflow_data["instance"]
    if not workflow.interactive:
        return {"error": "Workflow is not interactive"}

    workflow.next_iteration_event.set()
    return {"status": "next signaled"}
```
Once that endpoint is called, any phase currently waiting on await workflow.next_iteration_event.wait() will proceed immediately.
Passing Workflow Reference to the Phase

To let a phase call self.workflow.next_iteration_event.wait(), we pass a reference to the workflow when constructing the phase.
For example, in _create_phase:
```python
phase_instance = phase_class(
    phase_config=phase_config,
    initial_response=initial_response,
    resource_manager=self.resource_manager,
    workflow=self  # pass the workflow reference
)
```
And in BasePhase.__init__, we store self.workflow = workflow.
With these changes, the entire pipeline now supports pausing at each phase iteration when in Interactive Mode, and resuming upon a user-initiated signal.

### How to Test
- Start the server:
```bash
uvicorn server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```
- Execute the workflow with /workflow/execute/{workflow_id}. The workflow will pause waiting for a “next” signal.
- Signal the workflow to continue by sending a POST request:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/workflow/next/{workflow_id}
```
The workflow should proceed to the next iteration.
Repeat until the workflow completes all phases or you manually stop it.

body:
This pull request includes the following changes:
- Removes the sex ratio
- Sets data that cannot be expanded due to missing sample weights to a weights of 1.  This sets the expansions for those records to 1 similar to records with NAs (missing trip weights). This primarily impacts WA records which often do not have EXP_WT or RWT_LBS.  Since this has a large impact on the expanded composition data, this change should be reviewed carefully.
- Implements a vignette to show how sablefish data are worked up.
- Writes the composition data in a form that is more easily input into SS3 models and includes a bug fix allowing compositions to be created across a variety of data binning.
- Simplify function arguments:
  - writeComps now uses `comp_bins` for both creating length and age composition data.
  - deprecate `plot` input across functions and replace with `savedir` which allows greater control of creating and saving figures.

author: sampsyo
body:
Just a low-hanging fruit optimization for this op: instead of a `Vec<HashMap<usize>>`, we can use a single `BitVec`.

I did this in three steps and measured their performance on the chr22 GFA:

* Switching to a dense vector, but not a proper bit vector: 14.7 -> 2.2 seconds
* Switching to a proper bit vector from the [bit-vec](https://docs.rs/bit-vec/latest/bit_vec/) crate: 2.2 -> 2.0 seconds
* Reusing a single bit vector instead of allocating in the loop: no effect; maybe the optimizer already got this

Anyway, a quick profiling run suggests that running `fgfa depth > /dev/null` on this graph is now 90% printing stuff and 10% actual depth computation, so I think we'll call that good.

body:
This is damus' first algo feed.

## What's left to do

- [x] https://github.com/damus-io/nostrdb/issues/67

### Optional

- [ ] Switch over to token parser combinator 

I noticed I was missing many parts of the codebase related to column serialization. In an effort to have a more direct parsing style, I created a new token parser combinator.

## The algo

```
algos: introduce last_n_per_pubkey_from_tags

This function creates filters for the base our first algo in Damus:

Called "last N note per pubkey". I don't have a better name for it.

This function generates a query in the form:

[
  {"authors": ["author_a"], "limit": 1, "kinds": [1]
, {"authors": ["author_b"], "limit": 1, "kinds": [1]
, {"authors": ["author_c"], "limit": 1, "kinds": [1]
, {"authors": ["author_c"], "limit": 1, "kinds": [1]
  ...
]

Due to an unfortunate restriction currently in nostrdb and strfry, we
can only do about 16 to 20 of these at any given time. I have made
this limit configurable in strfry[1]. I just need to do the same in
nostrdb now.

[1] https://github.com/hoytech/strfry/pull/133
```

author: jsnmrs
body:
via https://htmhell.dev/adventcalendar/2024/25/
>For fonts you almost always want crossorigin="anonymous" on your link element, even when the request isn’t cross-origin. Omitting this attribute would mean our preload wouldn’t be used and the file would be requested again. But why?
>
>Browser requests can be sent either with or without credentials (cookies, etc), and requests to the same URL with and without credentials are fundamentally different. For a preload to be used by the browser, it needs to match the type of request that the browser would have made normally. By default fonts are always requested without credentials, so we need to add crossorigin="anonymous" to ensure our preload matches a normal font request.
>
>By omitting this attribute our preload would not be used and the browser would request the font again. If you’re ever unsure of how your preloads are working, check your browsers’ devtools. In Chrome the Network pane will show a duplicate request, and the Console will log a warning telling you a preload wasn’t used.

body:
Currently, coredump include incorrect code offsets, the generation relies on `func_offset()` which returns the instruction's offset relative to the function.

This change uses `module_offset()` to get the absolute code offset and, using a new method `get_relative_codeoffset`, converts the offset to be relative to the code section.

Also, the `name` property has been removed because it's misleading when displayed and not actually useful.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new Decentralized Autonomous Quantum Entanglement Experiment Coordination Platform. The platform allows for scheduling and synchronizing quantum experiments across multiple locations, provides tokenized incentives for achievements, securely stores experiment results, and implements a decentralized peer review system.

## Detailed Changes

### New Files:

1. Smart Contracts:
   - `contracts/experiment-scheduler.clar`: Handles scheduling and management of quantum experiments.
   - `contracts/quantum-token.clar`: Implements the quantum token for incentives.
   - `contracts/result-storage.clar`: Manages secure storage of experiment results.
   - `contracts/peer-review.clar`: Implements the decentralized peer review system.

2. React Component:
   - `components/QuantumEntanglementPlatform.tsx`: User interface for interacting with the platform.

3. Test Files:
   - `tests/experiment-scheduler.test.ts`
   - `tests/quantum-token.test.ts`
   - `tests/result-storage.test.ts`
   - `tests/peer-review.test.ts`

### Changes:

1. Implemented `experiment-scheduler.clar`:
   - Functions for scheduling, starting, and completing experiments
   - Storing experiment details including locations and status

2. Created `quantum-token.clar`:
   - Fungible token implementation for incentives
   - Minting, transferring, and balance checking functions

3. Developed `result-storage.clar`:
   - Secure storage of experiment results using hashes
   - Retrieval of stored results

4. Implemented `peer-review.clar`:
   - Submission and retrieval of reviews
   - Calculation of average scores and validation status

5. Built `QuantumEntanglementPlatform.tsx`:
   - User interface for all platform interactions
   - Integration with Stacks blockchain using `@stacks/connect-react`

6. Created comprehensive test suites for all smart contracts

## Testing Instructions

1. Deploy the smart contracts to a Stacks testnet.
2. Run the test suites using `npm test` or `yarn test`.
3. Start the React application and test the UI interactions:
   - Schedule a new experiment
   - Store a result for an experiment
   - Submit a peer review
   - Mint and transfer quantum tokens

## Future Considerations

1. Implement more advanced encryption for result storage.
2. Add real-time notifications for experiment status changes.
3. Develop a more sophisticated token economy with staking and governance features.
4. Integrate with actual quantum computing hardware for automated result submission.
5. Implement a dispute resolution mechanism for conflicting peer reviews.

## Security Considerations

1. Ensure that only authorized parties can start and complete experiments.
2. Implement rate limiting for token minting and transfers to prevent abuse.
3. Consider adding multi-sig functionality for critical operations.
4. Regularly audit the smart contracts for potential vulnerabilities.

## Deployment Steps

1. Deploy smart contracts to the Stacks blockchain (testnet first, then mainnet).
2. Update the contract addresses in the React component.
3. Deploy the React application to a hosting service (e.g., Vercel).
4. Set up proper environment variables for contract addresses and network configuration.

This PR lays the foundation for a decentralized quantum entanglement experiment platform. It provides the core functionality needed to coordinate experiments, incentivize participants, and validate results through peer review.

body:
### Implement Join Event

This PR introduces the `joinEvent` functionality in the event service, enabling users to register for events while enforcing several validation checks. It also includes relevant tests and refactors existing code for consistency and scalability.

#### Features:
- **Max Participants Validation**: Added the `maxParticipants` field to events and implemented validation for full events.
- **Cutoff Time Validation**: Ensures events cannot be joined after the registration cutoff time, throwing `EventRegistrationClosedException`.
- **Private Events Whitelisting**: Enforces whitelisting for private events, with `UserIsNotEventWhitelistedException` for unauthorized attempts.
- **Duplicate Participation Check**: Prevents users from joining the same event multiple times, throwing `UserAlreadyParticipantException`.

#### Refactors:
- Changed participant attendance status to an enum for better representation.
- Generalized the global exception handler to encompass all `ResponseStatusException` types.

#### Tests:
- Comprehensive tests for the following scenarios:
  - Event does not exist.
  - Event is full.
  - User is not whitelisted.
  - User is already participating.
  - Registration cutoff time has passed.
  - Successful joining for public and private events.

#### Additional Changes:
- Added `joinEvent` endpoint in the controller.
- Parameterized the server port in the Dockerfile for better configurability.

This PR improves event registration handling and ensures robust validation while maintaining extensibility for future features.

author: tarsius
body:
This pull-request moves metadata about this package from `-pkg.el` to `.el` and deletes the now redundant `-pkg.el`. The `-pkg.el` file is not supposed to be tracked in the Git repository. It is supposed to be *generated* by the package archive (e.g., MELPA) and *distributed* as part of the `-.tar` file. *If you are already convinced, you can skip reading most of the rest, but please read the last page.* ---- Unfortunately the [Multi-file Packages](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/Multi_002dfile-Packages.html) node in the info manual is not explicit about this. So you may have read this: > One of the files in the content directory must be named `NAME-pkg.el`. It must contain a single Lisp form, consisting of a call to the function `define-package`, ... and concluded that this means that your Git repository must contain such a `-pkg.el` file. If so, please carefully read at least the preceding paragraph again (emphasize mine): > Prior to installation, a multi-file package is stored in a package archive as a tar file. **The tar file** must be named `NAME-VERSION.tar`, where NAME is the package name and VERSION is the version number. Its contents, once extracted, must all appear in **a directory named `NAME-VERSION`, the “content directory”** (see [Packaging Basics](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/Packaging-Basics.html)). [...] This node talks about how a **package archive** (such as GNU ELPA or MELPA) should distribute "multi-file" packages as tarballs, and goes into the details of *what that **tarball** must contain*. It also mentions how that tarball is unpacked when a user installs the package. This node does **not** describe what files must exist in repositories used to develop individual packages. It does **not** say, that such repositories must contain a `-pkg.el` file. (But granted, it also does not say, that they must not contain such a file.) **Content directory** refers to a directory that was created by unpacking a tarfile. It does **not** refer to a Git repository. ---- The documentation lacks guidance on whether the repositories, used to maintain individual packages, should, or should not, track `-pkg.el`. So we have to turn elsewhere to answer that question. How do, or don't, the tools used to maintain the well known package archives use `-pkg.el` as a source of information? (They obviously all *generate* such a file, because that is a requirement, as we have seen above.) - `elpa-admin.el`, the tool used to maintain the "official" package archives GNU ELPA and NonGNU ELPA, completely ignore any checked in `-pkg.el`. It has always done that. - `package-build.el`, the tool used to maintain the much older MELPA, gets metadata from `.el`, but iff some information is missing from that file and `-pkg.el` exists and contains that piece of information, then that is used. Melpa has existed for a long time and when it was young, many conventions had not been established yet, and so `package-build.el` had to deal with a complex reality of many different, and often conflicting or otherwise problematic practices. So the reason that `package-build.el` falls back to using information from `-pkg.el` is not that its maintainer (that would be me) thinks that doing so is a good idea, but that it was once necessary and unfortunately still is. But now that only 1% of packages use `-pkg.el` without providing the same information in `.el` also (or preferable only), I am opening this pull-request, and four dozen like it, so that `package-build.el` can soon finally stop getting information from that file. ---- So why is it problematic to use `-pkg.el` in the first place? When the same information can be specified in `.el` and `-pkg.el`, then there are two sources of truth. This is not a problem as long as everybody always makes sure the information is updated in both places. Unfortunately, but not at all surprisingly, that very often is not the case. Many, if not most, package maintainers who initially put the information in both places, over time forget about one of them and stop updating it. To complicate that further, while most of them seem to stop updating `-pkg.el`, some instead forget to update `.el`. For a tool like `package-build.el`, that makes it impossible to always pick the correct source of truth, as intended by the package maintainer. I believe the only solution to this problem is to agree on a single source of truth. As a community we have all but done so already. Among the 5837 packages on MELPA, 99% provide the expected information in `.el`, while only %2 provide it in `-pkg.el`. This pull-request, and four dozen others like it, deal with the %1 that only provide this information in `-pkg.el`. Once these have been merged, MELPA/`package-build.el`, can start ignoring `-pkg.el`, just like GNU ELPA and NonGNU ELPA have always done. Once that has happened, the focus can turn to informing the package maintainers, who provide inconsistent information in the two places, that they are doing so, and might want to remove `-pkg.el`, to prevent that going forward. ---- Merging this pull-request addresses the problem for "regular" MELPA, the channel that distributes package snapshots. But doing this alone, does not address the problem for MELPA Stable. In the commit from which the release version is build, `-pkg.el` still exists and the information is still missing from `.el`. **So please also create a new release!** If you also tag your releases using Git, then please make sure you bump the version in both places. I.e., bump the `Package-Version` library header, create a new commit titled something like "Release version N", and do not forget to also tag that exact commit with the matching `N` or `vN` git tag.
Thanks for you attention! Jonas Ps: Please double check this pull-request before merging. As I have mentioned, I am opening four dozen such pull-requests, and it is quite possible that I made a copy-paste error in one or two.

## 🕷️ Add ScrapeGraph Tools for AI Agents Web Scraping

Hey guys nice framework! Added two new tools for webscraping using llm, tried it with `CodeAgent` and works like a charm ;)

This PR adds two new tools that leverage ScrapeGraphAI's services for robust web scraping:

1. `SGSmartScraperTool`: Extracts structured information from webpages using natural language prompts
2. `SGMarkdownifyTool`: Converts webpage content to markdown format with proxy rotation and anti-bot solutions

## Features

- **Proxy Rotation**: Both tools handle complex anti-bot protections automatically
- **Natural Language Interface**: Extract specific information by describing what you want in plain English
- **Structured Output**: Get clean, structured data from any webpage
- **Reliable Scraping**: Works on modern, JavaScript-heavy websites

## Example Usage

![Screenshot 2024-12-30 001433](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb1b2865-653b-4377-9ff0-44ad58a4e2c4)

The example above shows the SmartScraper tool extracting structured information from the Hugging Face Transformers documentation.

## Getting Started

1. Get a free API key from [ScrapeGraphAI Dashboard](https://dashboard.scrapegraphai.com)
2. Set the environment variable:
   ```bash
   SGAI_API_KEY=your_api_key
   ```
3. Install the dependency:
   ```bash
   pip install scrapegraph-py>=1.8.0
   ```

## New Example

Check out `examples/webpage_scraping.py` for a complete example showing how to use these tools with the CodeAgent.

The following is the output of Gradio UI:
![Screenshot 2024-12-30 001251](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f1d8186-a9ae-4ed9-9662-a073f80c7851)

Added `scrapegraph-py>=1.8.0` to project dependencies in pyproject.toml.

author: kadhirvelm
body:
At GAME_SLUG/GAME_ID/global, it now displays a special screen that the platform can use to display a "global screen". It's used to, for example, display the current standings of the game, the current clock, etc. It adds a new controller with a separate service to support this.

---

This pull request introduces a new feature for global screen functionality across various parts of the project. The most significant changes include adding a new `GlobalScreen` service, updating the backend to support this service, and integrating it into the frontend.

### New Global Screen Feature:

* [`packages/api/src/availableServices.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-eab97250cc59071dadea79b11e2c2bb877e4a1c04bc5b167dfd7c8331eaf31fdR7-R16): Added `GlobalScreenApi` and `GlobalScreenServiceDefinition` to the available services. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eab97250cc59071dadea79b11e2c2bb877e4a1c04bc5b167dfd7c8331eaf31fdR7-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eab97250cc59071dadea79b11e2c2bb877e4a1c04bc5b167dfd7c8331eaf31fdR28)
* [`packages/api/src/services/globalScreen/globalScreenService.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-e34aa5140a1fc1f6bd35616b28dcd72ae9b04dff859b79b5fb73108daa3b775fR1-R22): Created `GlobalScreenApi` interface and `GlobalScreenServiceDefinition` with an endpoint for `getGameState`.
* [`packages/backend/src/gameState/globalScreen.controller.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-42ce3cca5dcfb7566f610617c08f2f3c0adf7d06ec5c2f3dbacc531bb71ba973R1-R23): Implemented `GlobalScreenController` to handle requests for the global screen.
* [`packages/backend/src/gameState/utils/globalScreen.service.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-816db5e8abe0bd9ca5a44604a679e33eaddd211db8920d1c42d5ed67384f6f0cR1-R38): Added `GlobalScreenService` to fetch and convert game state data.
* `packages/frontend/src/app/[gameSlug]/[gameId]/global/page.tsx`: Created a new page component for displaying the global screen. ([packages/frontend/src/app/[gameSlug]/[gameId]/global/page.tsxR1-R22](diffhunk://#diff-8df7b9f91e740448042cab9ccf2c8b768930b6801d87ffe9ffd5a8a00f046c06R1-R22))

### Backend Updates:

* [`packages/backend/src/gameState/gameState.module.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-e8d141a10563b512838d65a506c7d9f3abb57e3fc63c83b26291e169edfb7bafR9-R21): Registered `GlobalScreenController` and `GlobalScreenService` in the `GameStateModule`.
* [`packages/backend/src/gameState/gameState.socket.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-1c6fdb4ee75c0c61a192c9a3ddb2287f6979e903aa50ce65936cb74e56c3de2dL40-R40): Updated logging in `GameStateSocketGateway` to use `playerId` instead of `socketId`.

### Frontend Integration:

* [`packages/frontend/src/components/globalScreen/GlobalScreen.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-c348e74ff7f400c85e9e535e45ff14fb9a8d058813ba407ae10ff0449c605c64R1-R49): Created `GlobalScreen` component to fetch and display game state.
* [`packages/frontend/src/components/globalScreen/GlobalScreenPlayerContextProvider.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-bdd382509b4521533df1bd3e64a16db20c1f21ff0a2d77ca515527c2e0256ae8R1-R25): Added context provider for global screen player.
* [`packages/frontend/src/components/globalScreen/InitializeGlobalScreen.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-b72750e8a2b4719f4d1b3de2bfe1008d80882341e6a63ce4587b39f6ba8b929bR1-R41): Initialized the global screen with game state and socket connection.

### Miscellaneous:

* [`packages/api/src/index.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-650ad1c40e291fd2a0f5ace33dd5e4a957e31f8d397fd4a5e5b75c0b50927f34R5): Exported the new `globalScreen` service.
* [`packages/frontend/src/components/player/browserIdentifier.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-e377930f0c496392cad44269d3ff02ac92989e6ec2a5d1a49fa0c156046330acR17-R32): Added a method to get a unique identifier for the global screen player.
* [`packages/games/src/frontend/frontendRegistry.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-6487ee791d71ff711da820fe4d521ebfb9ab8ce43d47768be50fa51479d60bb7L9-R13): Registered the global screen component for `the-stock-times` game. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6487ee791d71ff711da820fe4d521ebfb9ab8ce43d47768be50fa51479d60bb7L9-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6487ee791d71ff711da820fe4d521ebfb9ab8ce43d47768be50fa51479d60bb7R26-R40) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6487ee791d71ff711da820fe4d521ebfb9ab8ce43d47768be50fa51479d60bb7R58)
* [`packages/games/src/frontend/theStockTimes/StockTimesGlobalScreen.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-909c29e9267f08042e4e419e5b93fcbced8ad617635f60bbb72c5c528fe7c1f7R1-R14): Created a simple global screen component for `the-stock-times` game.

author: absidue
body:
# Detect and properly error on DRM protected videos

## Pull Request Type

- [x] Bugfix

## Related issue

- closes #6346

## Description

DRM protected videos cannot be played in FreeTube as that requires the proprietary, closed source Widevine CDM and a VMP signed build of Electron, both things which are understandably not included in the standard open source Electron builds. This pull request adds support for FreeTube to detect such videos and show a user friendly message (instead of it attempting and failing to play the DRM protected content).

Unfortunately the movie trailers are unlisted videos, so we can't just find the trailer some other way if it isn't included in the API response like they are for movies that are not free with ads.

## Screenshots

![screenshot-drm-message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8abc74aa-4509-468b-9c07-112c75aedfcf)

## Testing

1. Find a free with ads movie (e.g. https://youtu.be/3fE5uTeBGUM in the US, provided in the linked issue)
2. Visit the page on the local API, you should see the same message as in the screenshot

## Desktop

- **OS:** Windows
- **OS Version:** 10
- **FreeTube version:** c7c6dfd790c05e9e5e55a369f95d61eb7ca64db1

author: echowritescode
body:
Hi there! I noticed a crash on a particular chost from `@jessfromonline`, 971, so I went digging and noticed that it's because it had an attachment with a bunch of `:` characters in the filename. I'm using Windows, so this causes `File::create(&path)` to fail, because pathnames can't have `:` characters in them on Windows due to it being interpreted as a drive separator.

This PR just replaces `:` characters with `-` characters in attachment filenames, and specifically only on Windows.
